question: T12 (task-2cbf3dc7b70148a2): on the desktop, as CAP-T12SHORT H (presses 150, 60 and 0 leave 2 rows): does a drag that falls two steps or more in one move, on a 2-row Scrolling block whose 94 px line runs over its rows, keep the rows as a press does, and does the phone stack turn? On Blocks Probe at a 1600 by 1000 window, one new section per plan with a new Scrolling block and a second block added after it (desktop 1/2/3/26, and 1/2/3/10 for a Text block or 1/2/3/26 for a Scrolling block). Then 'open' (select the Scrolling block, Edit, Design), presses on Wave Intensity, a drag, 'go' (Escape and a press on the page) and Cmd+Z until as built. D1: a Text block; 150, 60, then a drag pressed on 60 and moved to 0 in one move. D2: D1 with a second Scrolling block. D3: a Text block; 150, then a drag pressed on 150, moved to 60 and then to 0, one move each 300 ms apart. Each drag's quick reads ('inputs') are read in the drag's own DevTools session, 80 ms after each move (and 400 and 1200 ms after the last) and 80 and 1800 ms after the let go. R1 and R2 are two sessions (probe-x.mjs in the lane folder), each ran D1 to D3 and T1, T2 of CAP-T12TABKEYS. Exit without saving each time.
readsAre: As CAP-T12DRAGFALL: layout of the Scrolling block and every block in its section (me: the Scrolling block; line: its drawing's height; sel: selected; kind; desktop and phone areas, top in the section and height), the section rows in the view shown, the Scrolling block's height, line (marquee and svg: top in the block and height), Undo and Redo, the panel's ranges; 'wave' is the panel's Wave Intensity value. 'inputs' holds each drag's quick reads (states: [name, { t: the page's clock, L: the layout as in reads, st: value, focus (isRange: the range has it), Undo/Redo, selected blocks, lines }]) and its events by the page's clock from the first (log: type, ms, the range's value). The read's name is the run, the plan, and the steps in order, '>' between them ('Z' is Cmd+Z, skipped when the section is back as built).
answer: D1: 150 takes the Scrolling block to 1/2/6/26 and the Text block to 4/2/6/10; 60 to 1/2/3/26 (2 rows, the 94 px line running over them) and 3/2/5/10, 10 rows. The drag 60 to 0 in one move keeps 1/2/3/26 and the Text block at 3/2/5/10, 10 rows, held at 80, 400 and 1200 ms and after the let go: the rows stay, as for presses (CAP-T12SHORT H). The line falls to 34.

D2, a second Scrolling block: 150 stretches both to 1/2/6/26 (twins); 60 takes the first to 1/2/3/26 and leaves the second; the drag to 0 keeps every desktop area, and the phone stack turns, the second first: the first goes to 3/2/5/10 and the second to 1/2/3/10 in the phone view, already 80 ms after the move. 11 rows.
D3: 150, then a drag 150 to 60 in one move takes 1/2/6/26 to 1/2/3/26 (the foot up by the fall) and the Text block to 3/2/5/10; the move on to 0 keeps them, 10 rows. A drag ends as the presses do.

Undo: a drag's Cmd+Z gives back other areas than the step before it (task-b4fedc8255866002): D1's first gives 1/2/4/26 with the Text block at 4/2/6/10, 11 rows; D2's 1/2/4/26 and 1/2/7/26, 12 rows; D3's gives back 150's 1/2/6/26. R1 and R2 read alike in every read and every quick read (areas, rows, line, Undo and Redo, the value).
Not read: a slower drag, a drag that stops on 30, the phone view.
